intro: To attach a file in ChatGPT on Mac, click the paperclip icon in the message box, choose Upload File, and select the document. The file appears in the query box, so type your question and press Return.
tldr: Click the paperclip next to the message box, then choose Upload File for a document or Upload Photo for an image.
Pick the file, check that it appears in the query box, type your question, and press Return.
No keyboard shortcut attaches a file. Option+Space opens the quick window, where the paperclip also sits.
The desktop app was renamed in July 2026, so menu names may differ. This page flags what could not be confirmed.
If uploads fail or ChatGPT ignores a file, test with a short plain text file and try a different browser.

blocks.text: Most people ask this with a deadline. You have a PDF, a spreadsheet or a photo, and you want ChatGPT to read it before a meeting. The steps are short. The menu names have changed over time, though, so this guide shows what each source says and where the gaps are.
Attach a file in the ChatGPT Mac app, step by step

The steps below follow iGeeksBlog's guide, which was last updated on January 9, 2026. MacRumors describes the same paperclip, but from the Launcher window. Both guides agree on the core idea. You click a paperclip, pick a file from the Mac file picker, and send your question with Return.

Start in the Launcher or in a new chat. Press ⌥ Space to open the quick window that MacRumors calls the Launcher. iGeeksBlog calls it the chat bar. Either name refers to the same small window. Use it for quick questions about one file.
Where the paperclip is and what its menu offers

The paperclip is the attach button. Click it once and a short menu opens. That menu decides what goes into your message. The two guides list different options, so the table below shows each one and where it came from.

blocks.caption: Options in the paperclip menu, as each guide describes them.
rows: A document, script or other file
An image file from your Mac
An open app window or the whole desktop
Your Mac camera, a webcam, or a nearby iPhone

blocks.text: Use Upload File for a document, a script or any other file that is not a picture. Use Upload Photo for pictures. iGeeksBlog lists these two options for those two kinds of file. If your menu looks different from the table, the names may have changed in the July 2026 update described below.
Upload a photo or screenshot to ChatGPT on Mac

The same paperclip menu can also take a screenshot. MacRumors says you can capture any open app window or the whole desktop. It can also take a photo with your Mac's FaceTime camera, an attached webcam, or a nearby iPhone's camera. That helps when you want to show ChatGPT a printed page without scanning it first.

Photos work best when the text is sharp and the page is flat. Crop out the desk, the cup and the keyboard before you attach. A tight crop keeps your question focused on the page. It also makes it easier to check later what ChatGPT was looking at.
Check the file is attached before you send

After you pick a file, look at the query box. The file should appear there before you type. If nothing appears, the upload has not finished or has failed. Do not press Return yet. Sending too early risks a question with no file behind it.

When the file is in place, type your question under it. Then press Return. MacRumors says that in the Launcher flow the attachment opens in a dedicated app window for follow-up questions. Ask your next questions there, so the file stays with the conversation.

Write a specific question. 'Summarize the pricing section and list three changes from 2025' gives ChatGPT a target. 'What do you think?' does not. Specific prompts help the model find the part of a long file that matters to you.
Which Macs and macOS versions can attach files

iGeeksBlog says the ChatGPT Mac app works only on Apple silicon Macs, M1 or newer, running macOS 14 Sonoma or later. That requirement comes from one source. OpenAI's help pages did not open for me, so I could not confirm it there. Treat it as the likely rule, not a guarantee.

To check your Mac, choose Apple menu > About This Mac. The window shows your macOS version and your chip. If it says Apple M1 or a later chip, you meet the chip rule. If it shows an Intel processor, iGeeksBlog's requirement rules out the Mac app.

On an Intel Mac, or if the app is not an option for you, use ChatGPT in your browser at chatgpt.com. The home page shows attach options labeled Add photos, Camera, Files and Add files. Those features require a login. Drag and drop works there for image formats including .heic, .jpeg, .png and .webp.
Keyboard shortcuts for ChatGPT on Mac (none attach a file)

items: ⌥ Space opens the Launcher, or the chat bar in iGeeksBlog's name.
Return sends your message once it is written.
No shortcut in either guide attaches a file. Click the paperclip with the mouse or trackpad.
⌘ Space opens Spotlight, so you can find and open ChatGPT quickly.

blocks.text: Option+Space and Temporary Chat are the only two shortcuts that either guide lists. Neither one changes how attachments work. Learn Option+Space first, because it opens the window that holds the paperclip.
The July 2026 change: ChatGPT Classic and the new app

On July 9, 2026, 9to5Mac reported that the old Mac app became ChatGPT Classic. It also said Codex is now part of the ChatGPT desktop app on macOS and Windows. The new desktop app has ChatGPT Work and ChatGPT Codex modes. The article did not say whether the attach and upload features moved.

I could not confirm where the paperclip sits in the new app. Both guides I read were written before the change, so their menu names may be out of date. If your window looks different, look first for a paperclip near the message box. You can also look for a control labeled Files or Add files, the same labels chatgpt.com uses.
ChatGPT Mac file upload not working: what to try

Most reports fall into three groups. Some uploads fail outright. Some attach, but ChatGPT says it cannot see the file. Some work in one browser and fail in another. Match your problem to a group before you change anything, because each group has a different fix.

The first group is a plain failure. An Apple Community thread from February 2026 describes the message 'Failed upload to files.oaiusercontent.com' in Safari. The original poster said Firefox and Chrome worked. Another user suggested the Mac may be managed by a work device policy.

If that is your case, check the browser first. Use Chrome or Firefox for the web version and see whether the upload works. If your employer manages the Mac, ask your IT team to check network access to files.oaiusercontent.com. Moving files to the Desktop did not fix the problem for the original poster.

The second group is the one that worries people most. An OpenAI Developer Community report posted October 28, 2026 cites build 26.1021.31345. The reporter says uploaded documents appear under Sources, but the assistant says no attachments are available. Replies in the thread say the problem also appears on Windows and the web. No confirmed fix is posted.

The reporter found that a new chat did not help, and re-uploading did not help either. To test the app, attach a short plain text file and ask for a one-line summary. If that works, the original file is the likely problem. If it fails too, the app is at fault, and you should write up the details for OpenAI.

A November 2 reply in the same thread reports an XLSX file that failed inside a Project, with the message 'Could not add sources.' The thread does not confirm a fix. Saving the spreadsheet as a CSV is a workaround I suggest. Try it on a copy, so the original stays safe.
Upload limits: what the sources do and do not tell you

OpenAI's pricing page describes upload allowances in general terms only. Free lists limited messages with uploads. Go lists more uploads. Plus lists expanded messages and uploads, with a Limits apply link. The page shows no file size and no file count. Read that link before you plan a large upload.

Third-party sites quote specific caps per file. I could not check those numbers against OpenAI, so this guide leaves them out. If a file is large, split it into smaller parts. Attach the part you need first, then add the rest in a later message if the first part works.
How many adults use ChatGPT, and who

Pew Research Center's 2026 survey found 44% of U.S. adults say they ever use ChatGPT, up from 34% in 2025. Pew changed its question wording this year, so the change is not like-for-like. Treat the figures as a rough picture of reach, not a clean trend line.

Use is strongest among younger adults. Pew's chart shows 61% of U.S. adults aged 18 to 29 use ChatGPT. The figure falls to 37% for ages 50 to 64 and 19% for ages 65 and older. If you help older colleagues with their first upload, plan extra time for setup.
Common mistakes to avoid

items: Pressing Return before the file shows in the query box.
Asking a vague question about a long file. Name the page, section or column.
Expecting Option+Space to attach a file. It opens the window. You still click the paperclip.
Trusting an old guide. The app was renamed in July 2026, and menus may have moved.
Using your phone as a fallback. Replies in the October 2026 thread say mobile uploads are not a reliable workaround.
Skipping the login. File features require you to sign in, according to chatgpt.com.

blocks.text: Fix one thing at a time when an upload fails. Change the browser, the file format, or the chat, but not all three. That keeps the cause clear. Note what you changed, so you can report it if the problem continues.
Where to go next

If you use ⌥ Space all day, read [How to use the Option+Space shortcut in ChatGPT on Mac](/how-to/use-the-option-space-shortcut-in-chatgpt). It covers the Launcher in more depth. For a wider look at the desktop app, read the [ChatGPT on Mac guide](/apps/chatgpt).

If you want to ask about what is on your screen rather than attach a file, read [ChatGPT voice on Mac and what it sees](/blog/chatgpt-voice-mac-screen). Those are two different routes. Pick the one that matches your task.

faq.question: Is there a keyboard shortcut to attach a file in ChatGPT on Mac?
faq.answer: Not one that either guide lists. The shortcuts they name are ⌥ Space, which opens the Launcher, and ⇧ ⌘ N, which starts a Temporary Chat. You still click the paperclip to attach a file.

faq.question: Why does my ChatGPT window look different from the guides?
faq.answer: The old Mac app became ChatGPT Classic on July 9, 2026, and Codex merged into the new desktop app, according to 9to5Mac. The guides I checked predate that change. Look for the paperclip near the message box.

faq.question: Can I attach a screenshot instead of a file?
faq.answer: Yes, according to MacRumors. The paperclip menu includes Take a screenshot, which captures an open app window or the whole desktop. Check that the image is sharp before you send it.

faq.question: What is the file size limit for ChatGPT uploads on Mac?
faq.answer: I could not confirm one. OpenAI's help pages did not open for me, and the pricing page lists upload allowances without a size or a count. Read the Limits apply link on that page before a large upload.

faq.question: Why does ChatGPT say it cannot see my uploaded file?
faq.answer: An October 2026 developer report describes this problem, and no confirmed fix is posted. Test with a short plain text file. If that fails too, write up the build number and steps for OpenAI.

faq.question: Do I need a paid plan to attach files?
faq.answer: The pricing page says Free includes limited messages with uploads. Plus expands messages and uploads. The page does not give numeric caps for any plan, so check the Limits apply link for details.

faq.question: Which Macs can run the ChatGPT Mac app?
faq.answer: iGeeksBlog says Apple silicon Macs, M1 or newer, on macOS 14 Sonoma or later. Check your chip and macOS version under Apple menu > About This Mac. I could not verify this requirement with OpenAI.

steps.name: Open the ChatGPT app
steps.text: Press ⌘ Space, type ChatGPT, and press Return. Sign in if the app asks. File features need a login, according to the chatgpt.com home page.

steps.name: Open the Launcher or a new chat
steps.text: Press ⌥ Space to open the Launcher, which MacRumors describes. iGeeksBlog calls the same window the chat bar. You can also start a new chat in the main window.

steps.name: Click the paperclip
steps.text: Look for the paperclip icon next to the message box. iGeeksBlog calls it the Attach icon. Click it once to open the attach menu.
steps.tip: If you cannot find it, read the July 2026 section below. The desktop app changed.

steps.name: Pick Upload File or Upload Photo
steps.text: Choose Upload File for a document, script or other file. Choose Upload Photo for an image. iGeeksBlog lists both options in its guide.

steps.name: Browse to the file and select it
steps.text: Use the Mac file picker to find the file. Click it once to select it, then confirm the choice in the window.
steps.tip: In one Apple Community thread, a OneDrive-managed folder was suspected, but moving files to the Desktop did not fix PDF and JPEG uploads.

steps.name: Confirm the file is in the query box
steps.text: The file should appear in the query box before you type. If it does not appear, the upload has not finished or has failed. Wait a moment, then try again.

steps.name: Type your question
steps.text: Click in the query box after the file and type what you want. Name the part you care about, such as a page number, a section title or a column.

steps.name: Press Return
steps.text: Press Return to send. Your file and question go to ChatGPT together.

steps.name: Ask follow-up questions in the attachment window
steps.text: In the Launcher flow, MacRumors says the attachment opens in a dedicated app window. Ask follow-up questions there so the file stays with the conversation.
steps.tip: Closing a window does not delete the file from your Mac.

shortcuts.action: Open the Launcher or chat bar
Quit the app before reopening it

troubleshooting.problem: Paperclip or Upload File is missing
troubleshooting.fix: Check you are in the ChatGPT desktop app and signed in. Quit with ⌘ Q, reopen it, and check your macOS version under Apple menu > About This Mac. iGeeksBlog says the app needs macOS 14 or later.

troubleshooting.problem: Upload fails with 'Failed upload to files.oaiusercontent.com'
troubleshooting.fix: Try Chrome or Firefox. One Apple Community report says those worked when Safari failed. If your employer manages the Mac, ask IT to check network access to files.oaiusercontent.com.

troubleshooting.problem: File shows under Sources but ChatGPT says it has no attachment
troubleshooting.fix: No fix is confirmed. Start a new chat, test with a short plain text file, and note your app build number. A new chat alone did not help the original reporter.

troubleshooting.problem: 'Could not add sources' with an XLSX file in a Project
troubleshooting.fix: Save the sheet as a CSV and attach that copy. This is a workaround I suggest. The thread does not confirm it.

troubleshooting.problem: The file type is not accepted
troubleshooting.fix: Check the format. The chatgpt.com drag-and-drop list includes .avif, .bmp, .gif, .heic, .heif, .jpeg, .jpg, .png and .webp for images. Convert other image types to one of these.
